settings.saved: Settings saved to the configuration file.

updates.confirm: Install {name} {version}? The plugin is downloaded and the wiki rebuilt; restart afterwards on the plugin page.
mail.help: Outgoing e-mail for notifications (new tasks, reminders, comments) and workflow e-mails. Messages are first written to the outbox and sent in the background with retries, so nothing is lost when the mail server is unavailable.
mail.inactive: No mail server is configured: messages are kept in the outbox and sent as soon as a mail server is set up (messages older than 3 days only after confirmation).
mail.transport_help: Automatic: SMTP if a server is entered, otherwise the sendmail program of the server (e.g. Postfix), otherwise keep the messages.
mail.from_help: Address of the wiki, e.g. wiki@example.com. It must be allowed to send via your mail server (SPF/DKIM).
mail.allowed_from_help: One per line; *@example.com allows a whole domain. Workflow e-mails may use these as sender; other requested senders are used as reply-to address.
mail.password_help: Stored in config.yaml. Recommended: ${EWIKI_SMTP_PASSWORD} with the value in .env.
mail.skip_verify_help: Only for internal servers with self-signed certificates.
mail.sendmail_help: Default /usr/sbin/sendmail; used when no SMTP server is entered.
mail.subject: Subject
mail.delete_confirm: Delete this message from the outbox?
jobs.title: Background jobs
jobs.help: These jobs run automatically. Here you can start one immediately.
notify.title: E-mail notifications
notify.no_email: Enter an e-mail address above to receive notifications.
notify.tasks_help: New workflow tasks for me and reminders
notify.cases_help: When a case I started is completed or cancelled
notify.comments_help: Comments on pages I created and replies in discussions I take part in
positions.show: Show the positions on the page

plugins.template_available: Available template – choose it under Settings or here

mail.enabled_help: Switched off, the wiki neither queues nor sends e-mails (e.g. test systems).
mail.disabled: E-mail is switched off: nothing is queued or sent.
mail.last_answer: Last answer of the mail server
mail.concurrency_help: Default 4. More connections deliver faster if the mail server allows it.
mail.rate_help: 0 = no limit. Many providers limit this (e.g. Microsoft 365 mailboxes: 30).
mail.bounce_help: Some mail servers accept a message first and report a failure later by e-mail (bounce). With a bounce mailbox the wiki reads these reports via IMAP every 5 minutes and tells the person who caused the message which recipients did not get it.
mail.bounce_verp_help: Uses bounces+m12r34@… so every bounce can be assigned exactly; the mailbox must accept sub-addresses (+).
mail.bounce_delete: Delete processed bounces (otherwise only mark them as read)
mail.old_pending: Some messages have been waiting for {hours} hours – please check the mail server.
notify.disabled: E-mail is switched off on this server.
notify.watches_help: Changes to pages and categories I watch
watch.mail_intro: Hello {name}, the following watched content has changed:
watch.mail_footer: You receive this e-mail because you watch this content. Manage watches: {url}
watch.help: You get an e-mail when something changes. Several changes in a row are combined.
watch.none: You are not watching anything yet. Use “Watch” on a page or category.
watch.mail_disabled: Sending e-mail is switched off – watches are saved but not sent at the moment.
picker.new_element_help: The element is created empty in {lang}; add content later with “Edit”.
feed.title: Subscribe to feed: {title}
feed.help: Paste one of these addresses into your feed reader (e.g. Outlook, Thunderbird, Feedly).
feed.personal_help: These addresses are personal: they contain a key that lets the feed reader read content with your permissions. Do not share them.
feed.profile_help: Feed readers and calendar apps cannot sign in, so your personal links contain a key. Renew it if a link got into the wrong hands – all previous links stop working.
feed.rotate_confirm: Create a new key? All previous personal feed and calendar links stop working.
feed.revoke_confirm: Delete the key? Personal feed and calendar links stop working until you subscribe to a feed again.
feed.setting_help: Offers a feed of the elements of this category (readers only see what they may read).
profile.card_help: These details appear on team pages that show your groups – only the fields chosen there.
profile.photo_help: PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP. Square images look best.
cache.enabled_help: Pages and API responses for visitors who are not signed in are kept in memory and served without database access until something changes.
cache.ttl_help: Limits time-dependent content (e.g. “Upcoming events”). 0 = until the next change.
cache.help: Signed-in people always see current data. For guests each page is cached on its first call and then served with a single request. Every change (pages, menus, permissions, users, settings …) clears the cache on all servers.
cache.per_process: Statistics are per server process; in a cluster every node has its own.
picker.source_new: Create a new category with this title
picker.source_help: The entries are normal pages of this category.
picker.store_in_help: The category decides who may see and edit the element. It does not matter for menus.
picker.new_source_help: Set the introduction and display later with “Edit”.

elements.help: All elements of all categories: search, filter, edit, move and delete.
settings.home_help: What is shown at /. For an overview of the areas use an element of the type “Category overview”.
settings.prerender: Prerender content for guests on the server
settings.prerender_help: Search engines, link previews and visitors without JavaScript get the title, description and page content directly in the HTML.
settings.preview_image_help: Used for link previews of pages without an own image, e.g. your logo or a cover image (recommended: 1200 × 630 pixels).
settings.guest_view_help: e.g. /, /e/12, /c/3 or a short URL like /calendar
settings.guest_unavailable: There is no guest view for this path (unknown page or not visible to guests).

watch.freq_instant: Immediately (a few minutes after the change)
mail.digest_help: For watches with a daily or weekly digest.
mail.digest_timezone_help: IANA name, e.g. Europe/Vienna. Empty: time zone of the server.

webhooks.name: Name
webhooks.category: Only changes in this category (with subcategories)
webhooks.secret_help: JSON only: every request carries the header X-Ewiki-Signature: sha256=<HMAC of the body>.
license.none: No license installed: without a license only private use by natural persons is permitted. Organisations (companies, public bodies, educational institutions, associations) need a license.
license.expired: The license expired on {date}. Please renew it.
license.over_users: {active} users are active, {users} are licensed. Please extend the license or disable accounts that are no longer needed.
license.key_help: Paste the key (starting with EWL1.) from the license e-mail. It is checked offline and stored in config.yaml.
license.remove_confirm: Remove the license key? Afterwards only private use is permitted.
license.terms: Enterprise Wiki is licensed under the Business Source License 1.1. Private use by natural persons is free; any other use requires a license. Each version additionally becomes available under the AGPL-3.0 four years after its release.
license.third_party_help: Enterprise Wiki contains third-party components under their own (permissive) licenses.

pgversion.recommended: PostgreSQL {recommended} is available and recommended (in use: {version}, supported until {eol}).

support of PostgreSQL {major} by the PostgreSQL project ends on {eol} (in {days} days). There will be no security updates afterwards. Please upgrade to PostgreSQL {recommended}.

Hello {name},

PostgreSQL {major} no longer receives security updates since {eol}. Please upgrade to PostgreSQL {recommended} soon.
pgversion.mail_howto: Docker installations: run "{command}" on the server in the folder of the installation (the old data is kept). Other installations: the upgrade procedure of your PostgreSQL installation (pg_upgrade).
preview_image.label: Preview image

acl.preset_help: Fills in the permissions below; they can be adjusted afterwards.
admin.role_permissions_help: Apply to all members of the role. Content permissions are granted in the categories.
admin.default_permissions_help: Every signed-in user has these global permissions in addition to those of their roles.
permissions.help: Choose a user, group or role. All categories you may manage are listed with the directly granted and the effective permissions and where they come from.
perm.core.categories.admin_help: Create top-level categories, move categories to the top level and manage the structure, settings and permissions of all categories (content only with editor permissions).
perm.core.users.manage_help: Create, edit, disable and delete users, including their profiles.
perm.core.groups.manage_help: Create and edit groups and their members.
perm.core.roles.manage_help: Create and edit roles, assign global permissions. Only administrators may grant permissions they do not have themselves.
perm.core.settings.manage_help: Site, languages, sign-in, retention and plugin settings.
perm.core.plugins.manage_help: Enable, disable, install, build and update plugins, restart the server, background jobs.
perm.core.mail.manage_help: E-mail settings, outbox and test messages.
perm.core.system.manage_help: Database, guest cache and system information.
perm.core.audit.manage_help: What is logged, retention and forwarding to other systems.
perm.core.i18n.manage: Manage languages and translate the user interface
perm.core.trash.manage_help: Permanently delete objects in the trash.
perm.core.elements.admin_help: List all elements with their short URLs and tags in the administration.
perm.core.watches.assign_help: Make users, groups and roles watch categories and elements (mandatory or optional).
audit.text_help: Searches person, action, object, IP address and the changes.
audit.what_help: Unchecked areas are no longer logged. Security relevant areas (users, roles, permissions, sign-in, settings …) cannot be switched off.
audit.log_logins_help: Successful and failed sign-ins and sign-outs, with IP address and browser.
audit.log_denied_help: Requests refused for missing permissions (e.g. when misuse is suspected).
audit.log_views_help: Who opened which page when. Creates many entries and personal data – involve data protection and the works council first.
audit.forward_help: Entries are continuously sent to other systems (e.g. SIEM, Graylog, Splunk, Elastic, Loki). If a destination is unreachable they are delivered later – nothing is lost.
audit.fw_secret_help: Optional: the body is signed with HMAC-SHA256 (header X-Ewiki-Signature).
audit.fw_headers_help: One per line, e.g. Authorization: Bearer …
audit.fw_help.syslog: host:port of the syslog server; TLS recommended. Every entry is one message with JSON content.
audit.fw_help.webhook: HTTPS address the entries are sent to in batches as JSON.
audit.fw_help.otlp: Address of the OpenTelemetry collector (e.g. https://otel.example.org:4318); /v1/logs is appended.
audit.fw_help.file: File name, e.g. audit.jsonl – written to the folder logs in the data directory, rotated at 100 MB.
audit.fw_help.stdout: Writes JSON lines to the output of the server (for Docker log drivers such as Loki or Fluentd).
draft.preview_note: Preview – this is how the page will look when published. Nothing has been saved yet.
draft.exists: There is a draft of this page (last changed by {user}, {date}).

publish.at_help: The page is then published with your permissions; until then it stays a draft.
publish.notify_help: Who watches this page or category receives a message.

publish.at_future: The time must be in the future.

notify.share_help: When someone shares a page or category with me
notify.mention_help: When someone mentions me with @ in a page or comment

wassign.optional_help: Users can unsubscribe in their profile.
wassign.note_help: Shown to the users in their profile (e.g. why they watch this).
wassign.profile_help: These watches were assigned to you by an administrator.
languages.translate_only: You may translate the languages marked with “Translate”. Adding and removing languages needs the permission “Manage languages and translate the user interface”.
languages.exchange_help: Export the texts for a translation tool or agency and import the translated file. Imported texts count as translated here; empty texts and texts marked as unfinished (PO “fuzzy”, XLIFF state “initial”) are skipped.
languages.export_component: Only the texts of the component {name} are exported.
languages.import_help: JSON, XLIFF 2.0 or PO; the format is detected automatically.
languages.imported: {written} texts imported, {unchanged} unchanged, {unknown} unknown keys skipped.
perm.core.i18n.translate_help: Translate, import and export the user interface texts in {lang}.
perm.core.i18n.manage_help: Add and remove languages, translate the user interface into all languages, import and export translations.
translation.original_lang_help: The language the texts were written in. Translations are compared with it: when it changes, they are marked as outdated.
translation.category_help: Title and description of the category in each language. When the original changes, translations are marked as outdated until they are revised or confirmed with “Still correct”.
translation.empty_removes: Leave empty to remove the translation (the original is shown instead).
settings.readable_urls_help: Pages and categories get addresses like /wiki/team/about-me, one per language (former addresses keep working). Off: /e/12 and short URLs only.
shorturl.only_help: The readable addresses /wiki/… of this page do not work; the short URL is shown and shared.
sites.help: An instance can serve several sites, each with its own content, settings, sign-in, plugins and permissions. User accounts, groups and roles are shared. The host name of a request selects the site; unknown host names show the site main.
sites.name: Name
sites.name_help: Lowercase letters, digits and _ (also the database schema site_<name>); cannot be changed later.
sites.title: Title
sites.hostnames_help: Comma separated, e.g. docs.example.org. Point these names to this server (DNS, reverse proxy, certificate).
sites.disable_help: The site is no longer served; its content and settings are kept.
sites.delete_confirm: Delete the site “{name}” with all its pages, files and settings? This cannot be undone.
sites.admins_help: Instance administrators manage the sites, user accounts, groups, roles, the license and installed plugins, and are administrators on every site. Administrators of the site main are instance administrators automatically.
sites.admin_unknown: Choose a user from the list.
sites.shared_notice: User accounts, groups and roles are shared by all sites of this instance. Here you assign roles for this site; instance administrators create and change accounts, groups and roles.
mail.ca_cert_help: Certificate of an internal certificate authority that signed the relay's certificate (PEM text or a file path) – safer than switching the check off.
sites.accounts_help: Shared: the users, groups and roles of the instance (rights per site). Own accounts: the site has its own users, groups and roles and does not see the others – for strictly separated groups of people. Cannot be changed later.
sites.first_admin_help: A site with own accounts starts without users: this local account becomes its administrator.
sites.first_admin_pw_help: Password rules of the site apply.
category.hidden_help: Not shown in the navigation, menus, listings and search – e.g. as a folder for media. Rights apply as usual.
media.library_help: Images, documents and other files of this site. Each file belongs to a category and has its rights; files can also get their own rights.
media.alt_help: Describes the image for people who cannot see it (screen readers). Leave empty only for decorative images.
media.category_help: The file gets the rights of this category (hidden categories work as folders).
media.crop_help: Drag a rectangle on the image or enter the values (pixels of the original).
media.delete_confirm: Delete "{name}"? Pages that show it will show nothing in its place.
media.download_help: Off: the file can only be viewed, also by people with all rights except managing it.
media.download_to_open: Download the file to open it.
media.no_steps: Add at least one step first.
media.not_viewable: This file can only be viewed in the browser if it is an image, a PDF, a video or audio file.
media.own_rights_help: Replaces the rights of the category and of the pages that show the file. You can only give rights you have yourself.
media.type.label: Type
media.unused: Not used on any page you can see.
media.wm.title: Watermark
media.wm.help: Burnt into images and PDFs. With the viewer's name, every person sees their own name – copies can be traced.
media.wm.uploader_only: Do not keep the original – only the version with the uploader's watermark
media.wm.uploader_view: Show with the uploader's watermark, original for downloads
media.wm.viewer_view: Burn in the viewer's name when shown
media.wm.viewer_all: Burn in the viewer's name when shown and downloaded
media.wm.uploader_only_warn: The original file is not stored and cannot be restored later.

office.editing: Editing – changes are saved as a new version
office.read_only_protected: Read-only, without download, print and copy
office.no_renderer: The browser part of this office program is missing (plugin active?).
office.not_configured: Not set up yet: enter the server address and save.
settings.viewer_help: Office files open in this program; what it cannot open, the browser shows. The details of a file offer further programs.
settings.open_external: Always open files directly in the default program
settings.open_external_help: A click on a suitable file opens it there right away instead of the details. Only possible for the default program.
settings.office_token_ttl_help: How long an opened document can be saved (default 10h, at most 24h). Rights are checked again on every access.
office.using: Connected via {url} (empty field: preset from the environment, e.g. Docker Compose).
demo.title: Demo content
demo.help: Creates with one click an area “Demo: Enterprise Wiki” that shows as many features as possible: pages with macros, Markdown, website building blocks, blog, FAQ, calendar with series and registration, team page with demo accounts (no sign-in, not counted for the license), media with gallery and watermark, files, workflow, page properties, comments, reactions, menu, text block and carousel. “Remove demo” deletes everything the demo created without a trace – including versions, trash, files and log entries. Your own content stays untouched.
demo.remove_confirm: Everything the demo created is deleted permanently, including your changes to demo content. Continue?
demo.reset_title: Reset the site to its first start
demo.reset_help: Deletes all content, media, files, versions, the trash, the log and the settings of this site. Only your administrator account and the welcome page remain – as at the first start. Address, languages, e-mail delivery, site name and license stay. On an instance with several sites and shared accounts the accounts stay.
demo.reset_warning: Caution: this cannot be undone. Make a backup first.
demo.reset_confirm: To confirm, type the name of the site: {name}
demo.reset_last: Really delete everything? You sign in again afterwards.
editor.heading: Heading {level}
editor.link_invalid: Only http(s), mailto, /path and #anchor links are allowed.
editor.image_alt_help: Describe the image for people who cannot see it.
editor.macro_none: No macros are available (no macro plugin is active).
editor.html_help: HTML that Markdown cannot express (e.g. merged table cells). It is sanitized when saved; leave it empty to remove it.
editor.help_visual: Alt+F10: toolbar · Esc then Tab: leave the editor · Enter on a macro or image: edit it · Markdown like **bold** or # heading is converted while typing.
editor.help_markdown: Markdown source (GitHub Flavored Markdown). Macros: ::name{key=value} or :::name … ::: with content.
profile.editor_help: Both editors save Markdown; you can switch at any time.
settings.editor_help: Users can choose their own editor in their profile.
editor.live_alone: Live editing: nobody else is editing this page right now.
editor.live_joined: {name} is now editing this page too.
editor.live_lost: The connection for live editing ended. You keep editing alone; changes of others are no longer shown.
editor.live_unavailable: Live editing is not available right now. You are editing alone.
editor.live_saved: Revision {rev} was saved by another editor. Your next save builds on it.
editor.live_saved_by: {name} saved revision {rev}. Your next save builds on it.
settings.collaboration: Live editing (several editors at the same time)
settings.collaboration_help: Editors of a page see each other's changes and cursors, in the visual editor and in the Markdown source.
editor.live_replaced: Others were already editing this page: what you typed before the connection was replaced by the shared state.
editor.mode_shared: Switches the view for everybody who is editing now.
email.confirm_text:
Hello {name},

please confirm that {email} is your address by opening this link (valid for {hours} hours):

{link}

If you did not add this address, ignore this message; nothing changes.
email.title: E-mail addresses
email.help: Notifications go to the primary address. Every confirmed address identifies you: you can sign in with it, and sign-ins of other providers with that address are linked to your account.
email.sent: A confirmation link was sent to {email}.
email.add_help: You get a link to confirm that the address is yours.
email.confirm_now_help: Only if you know that the address belongs to this person.
identity.title: Sign-ins
identity.help: Ways to sign in to this account. Further sign-ins are added when you sign in with another method using one of your confirmed addresses.
identity.unlink_confirm: Remove the sign-in {provider} ({name}) from this account?
identity.link_intro: You signed in with {provider} as {name}. The address {email} belongs to an existing account.
identity.link_how: Sign in with that account once to link the two – afterwards both lead to the same account.
identity.linked: {provider} is now linked to your account.
invite.title: Invite
invite.help: Creates the account for an e-mail address in advance. The person gets it, with these groups and roles, at the first sign-in with a trusted single sign-on that confirms the address.
session.title: Sessions
session.help: You are signed in here. End sessions you do not recognise, then change your password. Changing your password ends all other sessions.
session.end_confirm: End the session “{device}”? Signing in again will be required there.
session.end_others_confirm: End all other sessions? This session stays signed in.
session.end_all_confirm: End all sessions of this user?
mapping.jit: Create accounts at the first sign-in (JIT)
mapping.jit_help: Off: only people created or invited in advance and already linked sign-ins get in.
mapping.trust_email_help: A new sign-in with an address the provider confirms is linked to the account with that address automatically. Only for providers that check addresses reliably.
mapping.email_verified: The provider confirms all e-mail addresses
mapping.email_verified_help: For LDAP and SAML whose addresses come from a maintained directory. OpenID Connect tells this itself (claim email_verified).
authadmin.instance_help: Several providers of the same kind are possible (e.g. two OpenID Connect providers), each with its own settings, mapping and JIT rules.
authadmin.add_help: The id becomes part of the addresses and of user handles (name@provider). Do not change it once people have signed in with it.
authadmin.id_help: 1–24 lower-case letters, digits and hyphens. Provider id: {base}-<id>.
authadmin.id_invalid: The id may only contain lower-case letters, digits and hyphens (at most 24 characters).
authadmin.name: Name on the login page
authadmin.added: Provider “{name}” added. Now complete its settings.
authadmin.remove_confirm: Remove the provider “{id}”? People who only sign in with it cannot sign in any more.
authadmin.preview_help: Shows what a sign-in with these details would lead to: account, groups and roles. Nothing is stored. Uses the saved settings.
authadmin.outcome.existing: Signs in to the existing account {user}
authadmin.outcome.link_confirm: The address belongs to {user}: the person confirms the link with their previous sign-in
authadmin.outcome.refused: Refused: no account and JIT is off
scim.help: Directories such as Microsoft Entra ID or Okta create, change, disable and remove people and groups through SCIM 2.0, even before anybody signs in. A client may only manage people of its sign-in and groups it created, never administrators and never roles. Which roles a provisioned group gets is up to you (Groups).
scim.add_help: You then get the tenant URL and the token for the directory. The token is shown only once.
scim.name: Name
scim.provider_help: The provisioned people sign in with this. Their account is recognised then.
scim.subject_from_help: Which SCIM attribute is the stable id at the provider. Entra ID with OpenID Connect: externalId (objectId), and claim_subject: oid at the provider.
scim.renew_confirm: Create a new token for “{name}”? The current one stops working.
scim.delete_confirm: Delete the SCIM client “{name}”? The provisioned people and groups stay.
scim.token_once: Copy the token into the directory now. It is not shown again.
scim.no_provider: First set up a sign-in method (e.g. OpenID Connect).
mfa.none: No usable factor is available for this account. Please contact the administration.
mfa.by_provider: Further factors of your sign-in are handled by your sign-in provider (identity provider).
auth.passkey_cancelled: The sign-in with a passkey was cancelled.
photo.vis.label: Who sees my photo?
photo.vis.help: Without a photo the wiki shows your initials.
settings.session_idle_help: e.g. 12h or 30m; 0 = only the validity above. Automatic requests do not count as activity.
settings.photo_default_help: For people who did not choose.
settings.photo_max_help: Nobody can share their photo more widely. More narrowly is always possible.
settings.photo_fixed_help: All photos are then visible exactly as the default says.
perm.core.photos.view_help: See every profile photo, also those their owners show to nobody (e.g. for identity checks).
alias.label: User name (optional)
alias.help: Unique name in the wiki; signing in with it is possible too.
alias.help_self: Unique name in the wiki. You can sign in with it as well.
alias.managed: Comes from the sign-in method {provider} and is set again at the next sign-in.
alias.managed_self: Comes from your sign-in method and cannot be changed here.
mapping.username_from_help: Attribute, claim or SAML attribute that becomes the user name in the wiki (e.g. uid, cn, preferred_username). Updated at every sign-in; if the name is taken, the previous one stays.
mfa.title: Sign-in factors
mfa.chain_help: Your sign-in asks the factors in this order; factors with the same number are alternatives. A sign-in needs {required} factor(s).
mfa.choose_setup: What do you want to set up?
mfa.enroll_help: This sign-in needs {required} factors; you have {passed}. Please set up another factor now.
admin.reset_mfa_help: Removes authenticator app, codes by e-mail and security keys of this user; they are set up again at the next sign-in if it needs them.
mfa.admin.help: Every MFA plugin is a factor of the sign-in. Factors with the same number are alternatives; higher numbers are asked afterwards. Factor 1 (only plugins that sign in without password, e.g. passkeys) is an alternative to the password.
mfa.admin.factors_help: The number decides when the factor is asked (1 to 9).
mfa.admin.factor_help: 2 = second factor (default); 3 and more for a longer chain.
mfa.admin.factor_help_first: 1 = instead of the password (default for passkeys); 2 or more = additional factor.
mfa.admin.factor_invalid: Please enter a whole number from {min} to 9.
mfa.admin.enable_help: As which factor should it be asked? Factors with the same number are alternatives.
mfa.admin.providers_help: Which factors apply to the people of each sign-in method (instance), and how many factors a sign-in needs. Who has fewer sets one up during the sign-in.
mfa.admin.required_help: 1 = the first factor is enough (further factors only for people who set them up); 2 = at least one further factor, and so on.
mfa.admin.counts_two_help: The device checks the person itself (PIN, fingerprint, face): the passkey also covers the following factor of the chain.
sources.help: Elements of all sources are shown together, each once, and only to readers who may see them. Without a source: this category with its subcategories.
category.template_help: Look of this category and its subcategories – e.g. the CMS template for a public area. Without an own choice the template of the parent category or of the site applies.
space.help: Every top-level category is a space. These settings apply to the whole space with all subcategories. Everybody with the permission Manage here may change them – without administrator rights.
space.key_help: 2–16 letters and digits, starting with a letter (e.g. HR). Short address: {origin}/s/KEY. Leave empty for no key.
space.own_tree_help: Inside the space the sidebar shows only its categories and shortcuts instead of the whole wiki.
space.shortcuts_help: Important pages or external addresses, at the top of the space navigation. Wiki paths (/…) or http(s) addresses; the label is for the current language.
space.allowed_types_help: Only these types can be created in the space or moved here. None selected: all active types.
space.language_help: New pages in the space are created in this language unless another is chosen.
space.directory_help: The spaces of the wiki you may see.
archive.title: Archive
archive.help: Archived categories are read-only for everybody (administrators too) with everything below them, no longer appear in navigation, overviews and search, and can be restored at any time. Direct links keep working.
archive.restore_help: This category is archived: read-only, not in navigation and search. Restoring makes it editable again.
archive.above: A parent category is archived, so this category is read-only. Restore it in the archived category.
archive.confirm: Archive the category with all subcategories and pages? Everything becomes read-only and leaves navigation and search; you can restore it at any time.
archive.notice: This content is read-only and does not appear in navigation and search.
space.is_template: Offer as template for new spaces
space.is_template_help: New spaces can then be created with the structure, permissions, settings, website template and page templates of this space.
space.from_template_help: Takes over subcategories, permissions, settings, website template and page templates of the chosen space.
space.with_pages_help: Otherwise only the structure without pages.
space.import_help: Create a new space from a package made with “Export” (JSON Lines): categories, pages in all languages, settings and page templates. Permissions and files are not included; all content is checked like when saved.
space.import_below_help: Create a package made with “Export” (JSON Lines) as subcategory here. Permissions and files are not included; all content is checked like when saved.
space.io_help: Exports the space with all subcategories, pages (latest version of every language), settings and page templates as a file (JSON Lines) – e.g. to move it into another wiki. Permissions and files are not included.
access.help: The people who manage this area are notified if the content exists. You get a message as soon as they decide.
notify.access_request_help: Somebody asks for access to an area you manage.
notify.access_answer_help: Your request was granted or declined.
space.mine_help: Spaces where you, one of your groups or roles have permissions.
perm.core.spaces.personal_help: Create one own space (top-level category) that only its owner sees until they share it.
